claims.statement: Maven SNAPSHOT downloads are supported when enabled in the consuming POM or Maven settings; support does not establish a local configuration or authorize unstable dependencies.
This fragment points to Actions workflow GITHUB_TOKEN guidance; a link is neither a reviewed guide nor evidence of effective token permissions.

Package publication, installation and deletion require access tokens. Classic personal access tokens support Packages and API authentication with task-dependent scopes; the classic-PAT-only include must be read alongside the explicit workflow GITHUB_TOKEN paths, not as exclusion of those paths.

Within Actions, GITHUB_TOKEN can publish packages associated with the workflow repository. Installing another private repository's packages uses a classic PAT with at least read:packages, or GITHUB_TOKEN when the workflow repository has package read access. Scope alone is not a verified access grant.
The authentication step points to the containing page's authentication section; it supplies neither client configuration nor an authentication receipt.

Container authentication uses an appropriately scoped classic PAT, with token SSO authorization when the organization requires SSO. read:packages supports image download and metadata read; write:packages also supports upload and metadata write; delete:packages supports image deletion. No scope was granted or credential changed.

The upstream interface may select broad repo scope alongside write:packages; avoiding that extra scope, particularly in Actions, is recommended, with a host-conditional token-creation URL workaround. Saving a token in an environment variable is advice, not authorization to disclose or persist secrets.

CLI login targets ghcr.io for FPT/GHEC and containers.HOSTNAME for GHES, as resolved from the hostname include. Placeholder credentials and illustrative successful Docker output are not live authentication evidence; no example was executed.
For granular-permission registries, migrating Actions authentication from a personal token to GITHUB_TOKEN is strongly recommended upstream, not an adopted universal migration mandate.

Workflow REST deletion or restoration using GITHUB_TOKEN requires package admin permission and is public preview according to the included text, regardless of the beta filename. Workflow-publishing repositories and explicitly connected repositories receive package admin permission; this is not universal repository-admin authority or approval to delete packages.
